clue.text: Tiniest extremities lassoed by whipping, just before dropping off

indicators.note: something lassoed is caught inside a loop, so the whipping word wraps round the picked letters

parts.note: a whipping is a lashing
the outermost letters at each end of tiniest are both T

explanation.surface: A cowboy, whipping and roping the smallest calves, works on until the moment sleep arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just before dropping off' sounds like a precise timing but means at bedtime; the whipping word, a cowboy image, is LASHING.
explanation.definitionFit: The final act of the day, done at bedtime, is idiomatically the thing done just before sleep.

clue.text: One spotted that freedom in organisation's restricted

indicators.note: restricted means held within narrow bounds, so the letters sit confined inside these words

explanation.surface: Someone noticed that liberty within a company is limited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One spotted' reads as someone who noticed something; it is a tile marked with spots.
explanation.definitionFit: A domino is a tile marked with spots, so it is literally a thing that is spotted.

parts.note: a whimsical reason for a pill tasting comical: the old saying claims that mirth is the finest cure, so pills would be made of it

explanation.surface: A puzzled patient asks why their tablets have an odd flavour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'funny' means odd in the surface but comical in the cryptic reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb holds that a good laugh heals better than any drug, so pills made of it would taste amusing.

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird
bit is the past tense of bite, close to pecked at

explanation.surface: A bird has pecked at a tasty scrap of food.
explanation.definitionFit: A titbit is a small tasty piece of food, a synonym of a morsel.

parts.note: a bridge with an arched shape like a hump, and also a whale or salmon of that name that lives beneath the waves

explanation.surface: A puzzling question about a bridge built beneath the water.
explanation.walkthrough: A humpback bridge is a steeply arched road bridge; a humpback is also a whale (or salmon), the underwater one.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a sharply arched bridge and a sea creature, so an underwater one fits the playful question.

indicators.note: rank here means foul or gone off, read as the letters being spoiled into disorder

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A damp patch gives off a foul smell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rank' looks like an adjective describing the scent, but signals the rearrangement of MOIST AREA.
explanation.definitionFit: To aromatise is to perfume or give a fragrance to, so it works as the verb scent.

parts.note: the alphabet's extremes are its first and last letters, A to Z
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A blue river has been pushed to its limits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken to' joins the river onto the alphabet's extremes; read 'A to Z' then URE, the Yorkshire river.
explanation.definitionFit: Azure is the clear bright shade of a cloudless sky, a kind of blue.

clue.text: Bit of a looker secures prize, pocketing pound

indicators.note: pocketing means taking into a pocket, so the pound letter goes inside

parts.note: binds means secures or ties up
L is the abbreviation for a pound, from Latin libra
a pot is a prize, as in a jackpot or trophy

explanation.surface: A good-looking person wins a prize after stowing a pound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'looker' suggests an attractive person; here it is an eye, which has a sightless patch.
explanation.definitionFit: The blind spot is the patch of the retina with no light receptors, literally part of an eye.

clue.text: A tyke primarily entering competition to misbehave

indicators.note: entering means going into, so the picked letter goes inside the competition word

parts.note: a cup is a competition, as in the FA Cup

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so take the first letter of tyke

explanation.surface: A naughty child gets into a contest and starts behaving badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tyke' is a mischievous child, which makes the surface plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: To act up is an idiom for behaving badly, a synonym of misbehave.

indicators.note: converts as a verb means changes form, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Progress is made as a cleric ordains new converts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converts' reads as a noun (new believers) beside 'ordains', but works as a verb on ORDAINS.
explanation.definitionFit: Inroads are advances into new territory, so the word stands for progress being made.

clue.text: Twenty-four oarsmen, two (?) hours — patience is a virtue

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Twenty-four oarsmen, two (?) hours - patience is a virtue', gives ROME WAS NOT from an anagram of OARSMEN TWO, but nothing printed supplies BUILT; the '(?)' seems to stand for a missing word, and the blog cannot parse it either.
annotationWithheld.clue: Twenty-four oarsmen, two (?) hours — patience is a virtue

definitions.note: Girl's here is girl is, the possessive-looking s acting as the verb

parts.note: translated into Italian, will be is sara
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A woman's translation work is going to be difficult.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translating' tells you to render 'will be' in Italian, giving SARA; the 's of Girl's is 'is', linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarah is a common female given name, so it is an example of a girl.

clue.text: Piece of cake pressing black flower

indicators.note: pressing into means pushing inside, so the black letter goes within the cake piece

parts.note: a tier is one layer or piece of a wedding cake
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A slice of cake squashes a dark bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is a crossword joke: a thing that flows, i.e. a river, here the Tiber of Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tiber is the river through Rome, and a river is a flower in the sense of something that flows.

parts.note: to back is to sponsor or support
to pin is to fasten or secure

explanation.surface: Commercial backers lock down a deal at the tennis championships.
explanation.walkthrough: WIMBLEDON is the London grass-court tennis championship.
explanation.definitionFit: Backspin is a reverse rotation put on a tennis ball, a shot played at Wimbledon.

clue.text: Figure moving south: there's more to it

indicators.note: moving means shifting about, so the letters of south are rearranged

parts.note: and introduces something more, so this phrase gives and

explanation.surface: A person heading southward explains there is more to the story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' rearranges SOUTH to THOUS; 'there's more to it' is the conjunction AND.
explanation.definitionFit: A thousand is a number, and a number is a figure.

clue.text: God cuts tail from cuckoo and frog in half

indicators.note: cutting the tail means dropping the final letter of the word

parts.note: cuckoo means crazy or mad

indicators.note: keeping only half means the second three letters of the name are dropped

parts.note: Kermit is the famous Muppet frog

explanation.surface: A deity docks a cuckoo's tail and chops a frog into two.
explanation.walkthrough: 'God' tempts you to look for a named deity; it is the generic word for the creator.
explanation.definitionFit: The Maker is a title for God as creator of the world.

clue.text: He painted an image since then

parts.note: pic is short for picture, an image
as can mean since, as in as it rained
so means then or therefore

explanation.surface: An artist painted a picture after that time.
explanation.definitionFit: Picasso was the Spanish painter who co-founded Cubism, so he is a man who painted.

clue.text: Sentimental, weak, gutless individual caught in crush

indicators.note: caught in means held inside, so these letters go within the crush word

parts.note: to mash is to crush

indicators.note: gutless means with the insides removed, leaving only first and last letters

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one, an individual

explanation.surface: A feeble, cowardly person is trapped in a crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutless' leaves W and K from weak; with I they go inside MASH.
explanation.definitionFit: Mawkish means overly sentimental in a sickly way, a close synonym.

clue.text: Indicator of time given little help

parts.note: minute means very small or little
a hand is help, as in lend a hand

explanation.surface: A clock's pointer gets a small bit of assistance.
explanation.definitionFit: The longer pointer on a clock face shows the time in minutes, so it indicates time.

clue.text: Men suffering about son's unrealistic dreams

parts.note: chessmen include castles, also called rooks

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the suffering phrase goes round the son letter

parts.note: suffering means in pain

explanation.surface: Men in distress over their boy's fanciful hopes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Men' are chessmen, the castles; the 's of son's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names grand schemes or daydreams with no chance of coming true.

definitions.meaning: the number at 19 down is ten multiplied by itself three times, an example of a power of three
the painter at 21 across led the Cubist movement, which depicted geometric solids

explanation.walkthrough: One sense is the arithmetic power of three, the other the shape associated with Cubism.
explanation.definitionFit: A thousand is ten raised to the third power, and Cubist paintings depict blocky solid shapes.

clue.text: 1 seen off course, how much behind schedule?

indicators.note: off course means straying from the route, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: 1 points to the four-letter light at 1 down, the first word of that phrase

explanation.surface: A ship's position, spotted wandering, prompts a question about delay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off course' rearranges the 1-down light plus SEEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Lateness is the degree to which something is overdue, the amount behind schedule.

clue.text: This describes unidirectionality, that's for sure!

definitions.meaning: read literally, a single path forward has not a pair of directions to it
an idiom insisting something is beyond doubt

explanation.walkthrough: The literal reading of the phrase describes travel in one direction only.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means something is certain, while its literal words describe a single direction.
